fixes.explanation: Yes. Verses 17 and 18 say the high priest and his associates, who belonged to the party of the Sadducees, were filled with jealousy. They went out, arrested the apostles and put them in the public jail. Jealousy rarely sends anybody out to bake a batch of anything good.

Restoring the temple is a fair guess, but the apostles never say it. They are standing before the Sanhedrin, and they say God exalted Jesus as Prince and Savior “…in order to grant repentance and forgiveness of sins to Israel.” That's the reason they give. Nothing about rebuilding anything.

True! The apostles say, “We are witnesses of these things, and so is the Holy Spirit, whom God has given to those who obey Him.” So they stand there as witnesses, and they say the Holy Spirit is one too. That's a witness list with a very special name on it.

Gamaliel never says the Council might follow the apostles. He says, “…if it is from God, you will not be able to stop them.” Then comes his warning: “You may even find yourselves fighting against God.” That's the concern he puts in front of the Council.

True. Verse 40 says the Council had the apostles flogged and ordered them not to speak in the name of Jesus. Then, “…and released them.” I think that's a hard verse to read, so let's just say it plainly: the apostles were let go.

Close, friend, but the text has the number moving. Verse 14 says “…more and more believers were brought to the Lord…” and it adds large numbers of both men and women. That's not a crowd standing still. It's a crowd getting bigger.

Shadow it is. Verse 15 says people laid the sick on cots and mats “…so that at least Peter’s shadow might fall on some of them as he passed…” Peter is one of the apostles, and they're hoping for at least his shadow. When the hope is that small and still that bold, I think folks believed something big was going on.

True! Verse 16 says crowds gathered from the towns around Jerusalem, bringing the sick and those tormented by unclean spirits, “…and all of them were healed.” All of them. Not most, not some. That's like a baker pulling out the whole batch and every single cookie came out perfect.

That would be a plot twist, friend, but it's not what happens. The high priest and his associates were filled with jealousy, and verse 18 says they arrested the apostles and put them in the public jail. No invitation went out. The jail is where the apostles ended up.
Not quite. Verse 18 says the high priest and his associates arrested the apostles and put them in the public jail. Nothing in the text sends them out of Jerusalem. The jail is where they end up.

An angel! Verse 19 says during the night “…an angel of the Lord opened the doors of the jail and brought them out…” An angel of the Lord is the one who called me out of the junk drawer I'd been stuck in for years, so I'm a big fan. Locked doors don't stop the Lord's messengers.

That's it. The angel says, “Go, stand in the temple courts and tell the people the full message of this new life.” The apostles walk out of jail and are sent straight to the temple courts. That's not a quiet instruction, friend. It's a LOUD one.

Moses doesn't come up in their answer at all, friend. Peter and the other apostles say, “We must obey God rather than men.” Their answer is about God, not about a person. Priests aren't part of it either.

Spread isn't the word Gamaliel uses. He says that if their purpose is of human origin, “…it will fail.” He points to Theudas and Judas the Galilean, whose followers were dispersed and scattered. Both of those ended up coming to nothing.

Last isn't what Gamaliel says about a purpose of human origin. He says, “…if their purpose or endeavor is of human origin, it will fail.” His examples, Theudas and Judas the Galilean, both ended with followers scattered. Fail is the word he picks.
